subject: preemption of trajectory but not of resource

messages.author: a563d31d07937fcb
messages.subject: preemption of trajectory but not of resource
parts:
Hi, 

Perhaps this question has been answered before but I trying to find out how to handle the following case.

  1. parcels come in during the day and the warehouse closes at 18:00
  2. if a parcel is being processed at 18:00 by a resource then processing should complete. Other packages that have arrived before 18:00 should not handled anymore on the same day. 
  3. if a higher priority parcel comes in before 18:00 then that parcel preempts the parcel which is currently being processed.

Now there are some setups, each with different behavior:
  1. add_resource with preemption FALSE with a schedule: Parcels that are processed at 18:00 will continue processing until finished, but they will not be preempted by a higher prio package that came in just before 18:00
  2. add_resource with preemption TRUE with a schedule: High prio parcels will preempt parcels with lower priority, but processing will stop at exactly 18:00.
  3. add_resource with preemption FALSE and a separate task of high prio that will capture the resource at 18:00. This will lead to the parcel to finish processing, but also all other parcels that arrived before 18:00 will be processed. Then, after that, the high prio task will seize the resource.
Option 3 is almost there, but how do I prevent other parcels that are not being processed at 18:00 and that arrived before 18:00 from being processed? 

Cheers
  Erik

messages.subject: Re: preemption of trajectory but not of resource
parts:
Hi all, 


Here is what I came up with so far and this is working. The idea is generalizable to multiple resources. It uses do_parallel from simmer.bricks to close all resources in parallel at the designated times. 

The example uses a Bank with a single counter and two customers. The customers enter the bank at 17:00 and 17:30 respectively. These are quite problematic customers, each taking 5 hours to process (just an example). The bank closes at 18:00 but the first customers is served until 22:00. The second customer that arrived before 18:00 as well is served the next day. I am using one trajectory for opening a resource and one for closing a resource. 

Here is the code. 


# define resources and capacities only once. 
resources = c("counter")
capacities = c(1)

env = simmer("bank")
for (i in seq_along(resources)) { 
  env = env %>% add_resource(resources[[i]], preemptive=FALSE, capacity = capacities[[i]]) 
}

customer =
  trajectory("customer") %>%
  log_("Entering") %>%
  set_attribute("t0", function() now(env)) %>%
  seize("counter", 1) %>%
  set_attribute("t1", function() now(env) - get_attribute(env, "t0"), mod = "+") %>%
  log_("being served") %>%
  timeout(5) %>%
  release("counter") %>%
  log_("leaving")


openResources = function(resources, capacities) { 
  traj = trajectory("open resources")
  for (i in seq_along(resources)) {
    resource = resources[[i]]
    capacity = capacities[[i]]
    traj = traj %>% 
      log_(paste("Opening", resource, "capacity", capacity, "\n")) %>%
      set_capacity(resource, capacity)
  }
  traj
}

closeResources = function(resources) { 
  # closing resources in parallel so that closing will start for 
  # all resources at the same time. 
  closeResourceTrajectory = function(resource) { 
    trajectory(paste("close", resource)) %>%
      log_(paste("closing", resource)) %>%
      seize(resource, function() get_capacity(env, resource)) %>%
      log_(paste("closed", resource)) %>%
      set_capacity(resource, 0) %>%
      release_all(resource)
  }
  
  args = lapply(resources, function(resource) { 
    closeResourceTrajectory(resource)
  })
  trajectory("close resource") %>%
    do_parallel(args, .env = env, wait = TRUE)
}
  
bank = env %>%
  add_generator("customer", customer, at(17, 17.5), mon=2) %>%
  add_generator("closing", closeResources(resources), 
                from_to(18, 100, function() 24), priority = 10) %>%
  add_generator("opening", openResources(resources, capacities), 
                from_to(7, 100, function() 24), priority=10)
 


Please tell me what you think. Can this be simplified? How would you solve this problem?

Cheers
  Erik

messages.subject: Re: preemption of trajectory but not of resource
parts:
I think I might not have answered my original question. I am now defining the resource as preemptive and using the 'premptive' option in the add_generator call to make sure that only priority customers can preempt customers and that the timeout logic does not preempt. 

This should lead to the situation where a high priority customer (priority=10) is immediately handled, even when that requires handling after the normal closing hours (18:00). Then the closing trajectory which has higher priority (priority=5) than the normal customer (priority=0) should take over, causing the closing of the bank and the continued handling of the customer the next day. However, what I am seeing is that the original low prio customer is preempted by the high prio customer. Then the low prio customer is handled, and after that the bank is closed. Is this the expected behavior? 


Here is the code:

resources = c("counter")
capacities = c(1)

env = simmer("bank")
for (i in seq_along(resources)) {
env = env %>% add_resource(resources[[i]], preemptive=TRUE, capacity = capacities[[i]])

}

customer =
  trajectory("customer") %>%
  log_("Entering") %>%
  set_attribute("t0", function() now(env)) %>%
  seize("counter", 1) %>%
  set_attribute("t1", function() now(env) - get_attribute(env, "t0"), mod = "+") %>%
  log_("being served") %>%
  timeout(5) %>%
  release("counter") %>%
  log_("leaving")


openResources = function(resources, capacities) { 
  traj = trajectory("open resources")
  for (i in seq_along(resources)) {
    resource = resources[[i]]
    capacity = capacities[[i]]
    traj = traj %>% 
      log_(paste("Opening", resource, "capacity", capacity, "\n")) %>%
      set_capacity(resource, capacity)
  }
  traj
}

closeResources = function(resources) { 
  # closing resources in parallel so that closing will start for 
  # all resources at the same time. 
  closeResourceTrajectory = function(resource) { 
    trajectory(paste("close", resource)) %>%
      log_(paste("closing", resource)) %>%
      seize(resource, function() get_capacity(env, resource)) %>%
      log_(paste("closed", resource)) %>%
      set_capacity(resource, 0) %>%
      release_all(resource)
  }
  
  args = lapply(resources, function(resource) { 
    closeResourceTrajectory(resource)
  })
  trajectory("close resource") %>%
    do_parallel(args, .env = env, wait = TRUE)
}
  
bank = env %>%

add_generator("customer", customer, at(17, 17.5), mon=2, preemptible = 10) %>%
  add_generator("priority_customer", customer, at(17.75), mon = 2, 
               priority = 11, preemptible = 20) %>%
  add_generator("closing", closeResources(resources), 
                from_to(18, 100, function() 24), priority = 5) %>%
add_generator("opening", openResources(resources, capacities),

from_to(7, 100, function() 24), priority = 5)

bank %>% run(until = 100)


Also, perhaps this is getting too complicated and it would be better to add two closing generators: one at the exact closing time that does not preempt the customer (priority=5) and one 3 hours after that with a high priority (priority=30) that makes sure that the resources are closed. That would represent a more realistic case where the employee would refuse to do more than 3 hours of overtime. 

What do you think? I am just exploring the possibilities here.

On Fri, 1 Feb 2019 at 22:59, Erik Brakkee <erik.b...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I think I might not have answered my original question. I am now defining the resource as preemptive and using the 'premptive' option in the add_generator call to make sure that only priority customers can preempt customers and that the timeout logic does not preempt.
>
> This should lead to the situation where a high priority customer (priority=10) is immediately handled, even when that requires handling after the normal closing hours (18:00). Then the closing trajectory which has higher priority (priority=5) than the normal customer (priority=0) should take over, causing the closing of the bank and the continued handling of the customer the next day. However, what I am seeing is that the original low prio customer is preempted by the high prio customer. Then the low prio customer is handled, and after that the bank is closed. Is this the expected behavior?

It is. By default, preempted customers eventually finish their work,
and for that effect, they are handled in a special queue, different
from the main one. If you want to override this behaviour, you need to
set the queue_size_strict parameter to TRUE. Note that, in this way,
preemption may cause rejection (if there is no space left in the
regular queue).

For this problem you are describing, consider increasing the priority
of low-priority customers after seizing the resource (see
set_prioritization), so that they can be preempted by high-priority
customers, but not by the closing process, and at the same time the
closing process has a higher priority than low-priority customers
*before* being served.

Hope it helps.
